scope: Offline forensic description of retained seed17 goal-selected replay outputs and original calibration grades; fitting, calibration and development prefixes, no held-out rows
interpretation: First-failure classes are disjoint; reference diagnostics overlap. No repaired output is admitted or rescored.
interpretation_notes: First-failure classes partition the 412 rejected goal outputs. Reference-path diagnostics overlap those classes and must not be added to the failure total.

All 271 length failures remain invalid JSON after whitespace trimming. Long whitespace tails suggest generation degeneration, but retained outputs do not isolate weights, decoding, or their interaction as the cause.
The other 141 rejected outputs are parseable JSON that fail probability or source-grounding validation. Probability mass ranges from 1.04 to 2.94, so these failures are not rounding noise.
The existing implementation requests strict JSON Schema and then checks probability mass and visible source resolution. No rejected goal output reached candidate generation.
All 334 admitted outputs contain one goal hypothesis. Multiple simultaneously requested outcomes are not supposed to be separate competing hypotheses.

Teacher-reported missing constraints occur in 45 of 57 completed semantic disagreements. Eleven contradiction-only judgments concern an explicit no-request hypothesis versus the rubric's unknown label; this is partly a representation/rubric mismatch.
The completed-only 6/63 fraction is selection-biased descriptive context. It does not replace the original failure-inclusive 6/141 calibration result.
The teacher and annotation reviewer use separate requests/prompts to the same model, with zero human reviews. Their judgments are not independently adjudicated ground truth.
The four interrupted grading calls remain failures with unresolved original charges. They are not semantic disagreements and were not retried.

Compact source handles, deterministic probability construction, explicit unknown labels and joint-request coverage are hypotheses for a future experiment. This diagnostic changes no contract, weights, calibrated output or benchmark score.
